narrative.overview: A player keeps a spiral-bound book of key charts: cloth-covered board, photocopy leaves, a coil down the gutter, index tabs on the fore edge. This page is that book laid open on a dark desk. The world owns the frame and serves the column. Colour does one job: foil marks where the reader is, and nothing else.
keyCharacteristics: Cloth ground, paper leaves, toner ink; no third material.
Foil is a position marker, never an accent decoration.
Distinctions by rule, density and measure — not hue.
Chart apparatus at every scale: running head, folio, punched edge, index tab.
Square corners; the only circles belong to hardware.

rules.name: The Foil-Is-a-Place Rule
rules.body: Foil marks where the reader is. It may fill a tab, dot the wheel rim, or rule the masthead; it may never set a paragraph, a heading, or an icon.

rules.name: The Two-Material Rule
rules.body: A surface is cloth or it is paper. Nothing else appears.

rules.name: The Two-Script Rule
rules.body: Bahnschrift and Consolas carry pitch names, numbers and apparatus; Song carries running text.

rules.name: The Mono-For-Measurement Rule
rules.body: Monospace is used for counts, positions, durations and folios — never as a costume for technical.

rules.name: The Paper-Has-Weight Rule
rules.body: Shadows describe a leaf's distance from the board. They never respond to hover.

dos: Do keep foil to the current position: tab, rim dot, masthead rule.
Do draw every difference with rule weight or ink density before reaching for a hue.
Do set Chinese running text in Song and apparatus in Bahnschrift.
Do give each leaf its punched edge and its running head.
Do keep the reading measure at 34em so the column never widens past 75 characters.
donts: Don't colour the wheel, the staff, or any chord by key.
Don't round a leaf, a tab or a band.
Don't put a label above a heading.
Don't animate a hover, an arc, or a tab — motion is reserved for the leaf turn.
Don't use the grotesque for running Chinese prose or the Song for counts.
